Hi Morgan, thanks again for your comments on the chapter. I'm narrowing the discussion of trade and port cities so that it follows the people involved in a single journey before stepping back to the wider historical picture. I think that will give readers a clearer way into the topic, but I'd like your thoughts on how to connect that opening with the rest of the chapter.

I think it would be helpful to focus on the specific trade goods and commodities that are most relevant to the journey. This will help to make the discussion more concise and focused, and also provide a clearer sense of what the trade networks were like in practice. How do you think I should approach this? Should I focus on the specific goods that were being transported, or the routes and modes of transportation themselves? 

I was thinking that I might try to choose a few specific examples of trade goods, such as salt or spices, and explore how they were used and valued along the route. This could give a sense of the significance of trade in this region, and help to illustrate the connections between different cities and regions. But I'm not sure if this would be too narrow or too broad - I don't want to lose sight of the wider historical picture, but I also want to make sure that the discussion is grounded in concrete evidence and examples. 

Do you have any suggestions for how I might balance these competing demands? I'd love to hear your thoughts on this. 

I also wanted to follow up on your comment about the importance of considering the perspectives of different groups, such as merchants, sailors, and local populations. You're right, of course - this is a crucial part of understanding the dynamics of trade and port cities. I think I might try to explore this in more depth, perhaps by looking at the ways in which trade goods were brokered and negotiated, and the relationships that developed between different groups along the route. 

What do you think? Should I give this more attention, or do you think it's already well-enough covered in the rest of the chapter? I value your input on this. 

Let me know if you have any thoughts on how to proceed with the trade goods discussion. I'm open to any suggestions you might have.

I'm going to ask Shannon to coordinate a conversation between your head of product and our research lead so we can compare notes on the questions we discussed. In the meantime, I wanted to follow up on a couple of points from our conversation.

One of the points that stuck with me was when you mentioned the challenges of scaling your user testing efforts while still maintaining the quality of your data. I completely agree that this is a tough spot to navigate, and I've seen our team struggle with it as well. We've found that implementing a more robust analytics framework has helped us make more informed decisions down the line, but I'm curious to hear more about your experiences with this. We've started to explore ways to better gauge this concept, such as through A/B testing and customer surveys. Have you found that there are any particular metrics or benchmarks that can help you determine whether a product is truly meeting user needs, or is that a more subjective assessment? I'm particularly interested in hearing about any quantitative approaches that you've tried.
